61 people dead, one in five of the people who sustained stroke events, half of those stroke events within two days after injection.

A U.S. Secretary of State, Anthony Blinken held talks with incoming Chinese Foreign Minister, Xinjiang.
Days after China announced Xin as the new Foreign Minister.
Taking to Twitter, Blinken said that he held talks with Xin over the phone as he departs Washington for his new role.
The two discussed U.S.-China relationships and maintaining open lines of communication.
The talks come just before Xin leaves for China to take up his new post as Foreign Minister.
Xin replaced Wang Yi, who had been Foreign Minister for the past decade.
As of October last year, Wang has been promoted to the Politburo of the Chinese Communist Party.
Wang Sinyo corresponds to the rising tensions and between the two nations amid issues with Taiwan.
Wang is now expected to play an important role in the Chinese foreign policy as Xin takes his place and looks forward to building better relations between the two superpowers.
Joining me now to react is KT McFarlane, former Deputy National Security Advisor, author of Revolution Trump.
KT, what a pleasure to see you in person here in studio.
Happy New Year to you.
All right, what's China up to?
Ooh, China has every intention of becoming the new superpower in the world, replacing the United States and then rewriting the rules of order to its advantage.
And it's making no secret about it.
It plans to do this economically, technologically, militarily, culturally, politically, diplomatically, and it's well in its way.
But they are right now getting slammed by COVID.
They ripped the bandage off of that stupid zero COVID policy they have.
And they're stuck now with hospitals that are overrun.
They might have more than a million people die.
Isn't that going to affect their ability to do anything outside their border?
Oh, I think that actually it might have the opposite effect.
You know, Lenin, it was actually Lenin who said, basically, if you have a problem at home, create a problem abroad.
And then people will focus on the problem abroad and they'll accept what's happening at home.
So I think Xi Jinping becomes more dangerous in 2023.
And a problem at home, I mean, to put it in that phrase, when over a million people might die as a result of this COVID?
Yeah, but here's what happened.
You know, because China and Xi Jinping said, look, we're the guys who understand how to have an effective government.
Authoritarian government is how to deal with the modern world and COVID crisis, et cetera, et cetera.
They have no social safety net in the sense of health care that would be what we would consider adequate health care.
Their hospitals are being overrun.
And they have an alternative.
Can they lock the whole society down again?
They're having massive demonstrations and protests when they lock the people down.
And they don't just lock them down and say, we're going to give you a slap on the wrist.
I mean, they are having guns and people and guns going door to door to say, we'll shoot you.
They may not care about the humanity of this.
I mean, to us, thousands of people dying would be something we'd have to stop the nation for.
To them, a million people, that's just a number.
It's just a statistic.
However, they do care about the economy.
And they may have to shut down a lot of these, particularly the foreign companies that they have, the foreign manufacturing centers they have.
So, I mean, this could seriously affect their ability financially to, for example, their designs on Taiwan.
They might not be able to do in 2023 what they had been planning to do earlier in 2022.
That's right.
The knock-on effects of this COVID crisis will be big because not only will they have problems when they shut down their economy,
but other companies and countries are looking to say, we can't reliably do business in China.
We also have the idea that the United States is having an economic competition.
Maybe it's time to move our stuff out of China.
Maybe we move to Southeast Asia.
Maybe we move to South America.
But maybe we just move out of China.
So, I think that's also going on.
But Xi Jinping has made it very clear that he plans to have China have complete sovereignty over Taiwan while he is president.
And he's in his 70s.
So, he doesn't have a whole lot of time left.
But he's got a calendar and he's planning to do it.
And whether it's this year or next year or the next two or three years, but it's not 20 years from now.
So, he's on the move.
And he does now have Russian oil.
I mean, the Russians are saying, okay, fine, we'll sell our oil to China, maybe at a little discount.
But the fact is they can offload the oil that they can't necessarily sell in Europe anymore.
And today, you had this extraordinary video conference between President Xi and President Putin.
And I'm just, they were talking about a new world order that will be led by their two countries.
I mean, what's, how serious do you take all this?
When I was in the Nixon, Ford, and Reagan administrations, the whole thought of a Sino-Soviet, Chinese-Russian alliance is what drove American foreign policy.
We knew that was the nightmare scenario.
In those days, we thought that the Soviet Union was the dominant partner and China the junior partner.
Now, they plan to flip it on its head.
And the combination, just think about this, it's the combination of Chinese technology, Chinese money, Russian military, and Russian natural resources.
That is a very potent and powerful combination.
But that union never happened during the Cold War.
In fact, they fought.
And you even wrote a PhD thesis about that fight back in the United States.
